AN ARGON2 KDF PARAMETER. `timeCost` is the number of hashing iterations; it matched only because 'cost' is financial vocabulary. A SECTION NUMBER INSIDE A DOCUMENT PATH, not a figure about money. The line is `register: 'reports/campaign/P1_DEFERRED.md §2.11'`, the pointer C9 requires a deferral to carry so a reader can find the entry that rules it. Signal 2 scans raw lines for bare decimals, deliberately including strings — a rate written as '1.75' is still a rate, and narrowing the scanner to skip string literals would weaken a real check to silence a false one. The test this campaign applies — could this number, if wrong, tell a user something false about their money? — answers no: if it were wrong the citation would point at the wrong section of a register, which is a documentation defect and not a financial one.

$knownMirror: THE ONE THING THIS ALLOWLIST DOES NOT SOLVE, STATED RATHER THAN LEFT TO BE FOUND.
The display-copy entries above (purchaseGate.ts, ar.ts, en.ts) quote '₪0.01' and '₪999,999' as
literal text inside translated sentences. Those are the values of MONETARY_MIN_ILS and
MONETARY_MAX_ILS in src/config/financial.ts, written a second time in prose. If the bound ever
changes, fourteen strings across three files will say the old number and nothing will notice.
This is the same shape as every mirror this campaign has found: one fact, two homes, no
comparison. It is NOT repaired here because the repair is interpolation into translated copy,
which is A7's territory (the Hebrew fall-through audit and the single money formatter) in Phase
5 — and doing it now would mean rewriting fourteen translated strings without the formatter that
It is recorded so that Phase 5 meets it as a named condition rather than a discovery, and so
that a reader of this allowlist knows the entries are a deferral of one specific repair and not
a judgement that prose can never be wrong.
